question: A psychiatry trainee takes a detailed history from a 30-year-old man with a first episode of psychosis but focuses entirely on his presenting complaints, family history, and past medical history. Which domain of the psychiatric history, most distinctive to psychiatric practice, has been neglected?

answers.text: Social and developmental history, including premorbid personality, occupational function, and substance use history.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The social and developmental history — including premorbid personality, level of functioning before illness, substance use, and social circumstances — is the domain most distinctive to psychiatric history-taking and most frequently under-elicited by physicians trained in general medicine. It is indispensable for formulation and management planning.
Incorrect. Chief complaint and duration were covered (presenting complaints). The gap is in the social and developmental domain.
Incorrect. These domains were explicitly taken by the trainee. The neglected domain is social, developmental, and premorbid personality history.
Incorrect. Physical examination is important but is not a domain of the psychiatric history; it is a separate clinical assessment step.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the psychiatric history structure section. Identify which domains are most distinctive to psychiatry beyond the standard medical history template.

Well identified. Premorbid personality, social circumstances, and substance use history are the diagnostic and prognostic backbone of psychiatric formulation — and the most commonly neglected domains in non-psychiatric settings.
